text:
morgan: quick RFC follow-up. two egress patterns on the table: lightweight passthrough relays (ephemeral shim) vs per-tenant source-affinity (preserve src IP). want to document tradeoffs before we lock the default.

irene: missed the main thread. concrete differences?

morgan: shim = short-lived relays fronting outbound egress, we SNAT into a shared pool. cheap baseline and scales easily. affinity = provision per-tenant egress (ENI or dedicated NAT IP) so partner firewalls see customer srcIP. higher infra & quota footprint.

sam: ops notes: shim = stateless pods behind LB, easy autoscale and ramp. affinity needs provisioning plumbing and quota monitoring. shim will break IP-based allowlists.

alex: security/compliance: many partners only support IP allowlisting. header-based tenant IDs help tracing but don't satisfy those partners. Also need to think about TLS handling.

jay: exactly. some finance customers will refuse anything but preserved IP.

kat: rough cost delta we modeled for 400-600 tenants: shim ~ $5-7k/mo, affinity ~ $18-25k/mo (ENI-per-tenant model). latency: shim median +7-12ms, p95 up to +25-40ms depending on region.

ops-bot: cost_latency_snapshot: tenants=500; shim_monthly=$6.1k; affinity_monthly=$21.8k; shim_median_latency=+9ms; shim_p95_latency=+33ms.

irene: p95 +33ms could violate sync SLO for some integrations. can we micro-optimize shim to drop p95?

sam: yes1: colocate shim relays per region and enable long-lived upstream connections and connection pooling. 2: tune instance sizes and tcp_keepalive. we've seen p95 drop ~15-20ms in tests.

alex: TLS: options are L4 passthrough (keep SNI intact) or L7 terminate (we can inject headers/caching). L7 gives more features but increases cert ops and may break partner SNI routing.

jay: prefer L4 passthrough for shim. fewer compatibility surprises.

kat: product suggestion: default = ephemeral shim (L4 passthrough) for all hosted tenants. offer a paid "preserve-srcip" enterprise addon which provisions either: (A) per-tenant ENI/NAT (strong isolation), or (B) mapped egress IPs from a pooled gateway (cheaper, more mapping ops).

morgan: that would let us keep baseline costs low and still meet enterprise needs. need to decide default fallback behavior for affinity: if the customer's affinity path becomes unhealthy, do we fail-closed (block outbound) or fail-open (route via shim)?

irene: recommend fail-closed by default for preserve-srcip, with explicit opt-in to fail-open. must show this in onboarding UI.

sam: runbook essentials for shim: region/az autoscaling groups, circuit-breaker to avoid cascading egress storms, metrics: per-tenant egress_bytes, snat_assigned_count, instance_conn_reuse_ratio, plus trace header propagation (X-Redwood-Trace).

alex: affinity implementation detail: ENI-per-tenant gives true srcip preservation and is easiest to audit, but hits AWS ENI/NAT quotas fast. pooled-IP NAT with strict mapping is lower-cost but we must build robust IP reassignment automation and SLAs for IP stickiness.

jay: customers may request dedicated IP ranges; we should support both and document tradeoffs to sales.

kat: compliance note: for SOC/PCI customers, dedicated ENI/NAT is easier to justify. pooled IPs are OK for less-regulated customers if we provide auditable assignment logs and contractual guarantees.

morgan: prototype notes: stick with passthrough shim using tproxy+haproxy to get connection reuse without touching TLS. sample tproxy redirect we used in spike (ops implementors, capture in runtime docs):

# tproxy redirection snippet (example)
ip rule add fwmark 1 lookup 100
ip route add local 0.0.0.0/0 dev lo table 100
iptables -t mangle -N RDR_TPROXY
iptables -t mangle -A PREROUTING -p tcp -j RDR_TPROXY
iptables -t mangle -A RDR_TPROXY -p tcp -m mark --mark 0 -j TPROXY --on-port 15001 --tproxy-mark 0x1/0x1

This keeps L4 passthrough and lets haproxy reuse upstream sockets.

sam: i'll put a staging job up to run perf at 5k conn/s and measure median/p95 with and without pooling.

irene: ops will draft provisioning + deprovisioning playbooks for preserve-srcip addon and include quota checks, health probes, and rollback steps. also define retention window for audit logs.

kat: product/finance will draft addon pricing bands (per-tenant fixed + per-GB egress) and margin targets; legal to review IP assignment SLA language.

morgan: decision path proposed:
- default: ephemeral-shim (L4 passthrough) for hosted tenants.
- enterprise addon: preserve-srcip with two implementation choices (ENI-per-tenant or pooled-ip NAT).
- preserve-srcip default failure policy = fail-closed unless customer opts into fail-open.
- perf optimizations: regional relay placement + conn pooling to reduce p95.

alex: fine with that. please add explicit docs on SNI implications if we ever consider L7 terminate.

jay: +1. also include customer onboarding checklist for IP allowlisting timelines.
